Elena — thanks for the digest and the quick heads-up. I’m escalating this to our incident triage and looped Sean (on-call infra) and Monica (CS lead) to coordinate.

Immediate notes / asks:
- We see the same 429/504 patterns in our top-level metrics (latency + 5xx up ~6x in last 30m).
- Please do not change client backoff aggressively yet — small random jitter + exponential backoff is fine. We want to avoid a synchronized retry storm.

Temporary mitigations we can push in ~15–30m from our side (I'll confirm ETA):
1) Soft client-side advisory: suggest CloudClinic reduce concurrent streams per session from 4 -> 2 and increase keepalive interval to 45s. (Non-blocking; we can provide a short patch for you to deploy.)
2) Route new traffic to a dedicated shard for CloudClinic for 2 hours (if capacity allows) to prevent noisy-neighbor amplification.
3) Introduce a short-lived 207 'rate advisory' header so clients back off more gently (safe fallback).

I'll run the infra checks now and follow up with a concrete mitigation timeline. Attaching the initial digest you sent into our incident record.

—Marissa

Hi Jonas/Monica — forwarding the CloudClinic report. Severity is P1 for them (paying multi-region account). Current hypothesis: transient ingress pressure + aggressive client retry amplification => keepalive / idle disconnects that appear as upstream 504/429. We need exec visibility because SLA exposure is real and we may need reserved capacity or emergency credits if this persists.

Quick summary of proposed immediate interventions (I'll own coordination):
A) Short-term (next 1 hour):
 - Apply per-customer soft-shard routing for CloudClinic to isolate load (risk: limited spare capacity).
 - Deploy rate-advisory header + soft throttle config (no code change for client) to reduce retry bursts.
 - Recommend CloudClinic implement client advisory: concurrent streams 2, keepalive 45s, randomized backoff with max 8s. (We can provide a tiny patch; I've asked them to hold changes until we confirm our server-side knobs.)

B) Medium-term (24–72h):
 - Investigate kernel-level TCP keepalive defaults + idle stream GC in our streaming runtime (possible regression with new kernel optimizations rolled last week).
 - Enable temporary higher connection backlog for affected environments and add additional autoscale headroom for streaming shards.

Action items and owners:
 - Sean Gallagher: validate shard isolation capacity + deploy advisory header (ETA 30m) — seang
 - Marissa Cole: coordinate comms + client advisory + runbook update (ETA 1h) — marissa
 - Jonas Weber: approve emergency reserved capacity if shard shift causes saturation (please confirm by 08:30 PT) — jonas
 - Monica Patel: coordinate CS credit approval if SLA is impacted (please standby) — monica

Confidence: Medium (we have matching telemetry but need logs from the streaming runtime). If Jonas approves, we can do shard routing within ~20 minutes and see if rates normalize.
